title: Process Customers in Waiting Order
real_world_story: A bank branch receives customers waiting for services such as cash withdrawal, deposits, and account enquiries. Customers must be served in the same order in which they join the waiting line.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Customer IDs entering the service queue
real_world_connection.target_represents: Order in which customers should be served
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A queue that processes the customer who arrived first before later customers

problem_statement: Given N customer IDs in the order in which they enter a bank service queue, process all customers using FIFO ordering and print their IDs in the order in which they are served.
task: Process every customer in the same order in which they joined the queue.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of customers. The second line contains N space-separated customer IDs.
output_format: Print the customer IDs in their service order separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: Customers are served in the same order in which they entered the waiting queue.
Customer 72 arrived first and is therefore served before the remaining customers.

expected_algorithm.name: Queue Operations
expected_algorithm.reason: A queue follows First-In-First-Out ordering, which matches the required customer service order.

hint: Add customers to the queue in their arrival order.
Remove the customer from the front of the queue.
Continue until the queue becomes empty.
Print each customer when it is served.
real_world_takeaway: Queue operations help banks manage waiting customers fairly by ensuring that earlier arrivals are normally served before later arrivals.
